newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares continue strong run.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares continue strong run.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares stuck firmly on a bullish course on Tuesday, leaping 80.1 points to 6,590.08 on the main 57-counter industrial index amid heavy investment support and positional buying, brokers said.
"The market is very active, very firm and quite a number of players are in the field now amid perceptions that shares will be hard to come by in coming months," one broker commented.
"The short-term outlook is one of optimism," he said.

Trade on the Zimbabwean Stock Exchange has risen significantly since last week when the central Reserve Bank raised to 40 percent from 35 percent the amount of equity foreigners were allowed to buy in a Zimbabwean company.

On Tuesday, brokers reported large volumes traded on the industrial portfolio, with key counters including sugar producer Hippo Valley (20 cents up at 780), timber group Border (also 20 cents higher at 1,400), Zimbabwe Sugar Refinery-ZSR (90 cents up at 1,090) and financial credit-support house udc (also 20 cents higher at 220), all rising to maintain the bullish trend.

In minings, nickel miner Bindura gained 70 cents to 1,150 and gold producer Ashanti jumped 1,000 to 16,000, helping to push the secondary seven-share mining index 5.69 points higher on the day. It closed at 1,403.11.
